trade.tactic: RangeMe, Metcash and Partner Hub paperwork
trade.detail: Coles reads RangeMe before category reviews; Woolworths takes submissions through Partner Hub against its Range Review Calendar; Metcash's food portal reopens 26 October. All three lodged before the boxes go out
trade.why: The majors range once or twice a year by calendar. Nothing sent in November lands in February unless the paperwork is already in their systems; a box alone is a sample, a profile is a candidate.

trade.detail: 40 boxes to named buyers: Coles and Coles Local, Woolworths and Metro, Metcash and IGA state category managers in Victoria, NSW, Queensland and South Australia, Ritchies, Harris Farm (gourmet grocery inbox), David Jones Food, Leo's Fine Food, FoodWorks, Dan Murphy's (as a separate cocktail-syrup conversation), and 20 independent delis, gourmet grocers and specialty distributors in Victoria
trade.why: A buyer decides with their mouth. A bottle on the desk is the only medium that gets tasted. Forty boxes cost less than one trade-magazine page, and the independents among them are the listings that can be on shelf by February.

trade.detail: Santo Romeo phones every box recipient ten days after delivery; meetings before 18 December or in the January round
trade.why: Boxes without a call are gifts. The call turns a sample into a range review date.

trade.detail: Six posts in Santo's name, weekly from 16 November then fortnightly; comments answered same day
trade.why: Category managers live on LinkedIn during work hours. A founder's own words outperform a brand page every time the platform has measured it.

trade.tactic: LinkedIn, sponsored posts to buyer titles
trade.detail: Thought-leader ads promoting posts 1, 3 and 5 to category, buying and merchandise titles at the named retailers; one Sales Navigator seat for three months
trade.why: The audience is a few hundred people. Paying to reach exactly them is cheaper than reaching everyone.

trade.detail: Release to Inside FMCG, Retail World, Australian Food News, Food & Drink Business, C&I and The Shout; individual pitches with a bottle to each editor
trade.why: A buyer who has read about the product before the box arrives opens the box. Trade editors want new Australian lines; the import angle is a story.

trade.detail: Santo offered to FMCG and grocery podcasts for a recorded conversation in November or January
trade.why: Thirty minutes of a founder talking is worth more to a buyer than any advertisement, and the audio is reused in social for a year.

trade.tactic: Trade page, sell sheet, specification sheet
trade.detail: Trade page on the website with downloadable sell sheet, specification, barcodes and shelf artwork; 200 printed sell sheets
trade.why: The box sends them somewhere. The page is where the buyer's assistant finds the case dimensions at 4 pm on a Friday.

trade.tactic: Instagram, Facebook and X, feed build
trade.detail: Three posts a week from 16 November so the feed a buyer checks looks like a brand that is already selling; $300 a month to boost the best
trade.why: Every buyer looks at the Instagram account before replying. An account with 40 posts and real engagement is proof of demand; an empty one is a reason to say no.

trade.detail: Convenience and Impulse Retailing Expo, 16 and 17 March 2027, MCEC; free for buyers, independent grocery and convenience. A shared or small stand if budget extends, otherwise Santo walks the floor with bottles
trade.why: The first trade floor inside the campaign window where independent grocery buyers gather. Fine Food Australia is not until September 2027 in Sydney.

consumer.detail: Twelve tasting days across ranging Ritchies and IGA stores in Melbourne and the Goulburn Valley, Saturdays from 20 February; yoghurt and blue cheese on the spoon
consumer.why: Tasting is the one medium that converts on the spot. Fig syrup on blue cheese sells itself; nobody buys an unknown syrup from a shelf talker alone.

consumer.detail: A shelf talker under every facing, a recipe card at every tasting and in every online order
consumer.why: The shopper is standing in front of maple. Six words tell them this is the same use and grown in Victoria.

consumer.tactic: Consumer media release and writer seeding
consumer.detail: Release on 15 February; 25 kits (bottle, figs, story card) to Broadsheet's Dan Cunningham and Laura Box, Good Food, Herald Sun Taste (Kara Monssen), Country Style (Kylie Imeson), Gourmet Traveller, delicious., Time Out Melbourne (Rushani Epa), Richard Cornish, Dani Valent, Jill Dupleix and Lee Tran Lam
consumer.why: February is fig season in every food section. A new Victorian fig product is the easiest pitch of the year to land.

consumer.detail: Saturday 13 March, inside the Melbourne Food and Wine Festival window of 5 to 21 March; twenty seats for writers, podcasters and buyers, coach from Melbourne, the family cooking under the trees
consumer.why: The orchard in harvest is the brand's one unrepeatable asset. One day there produces more coverage than a month of emails, and the buyers who come leave as advocates.

consumer.tactic: Recipe creators, seeded and four paid
consumer.detail: 25 Victorian food creators of 10,000 to 80,000 followers seeded from 1 February; four paid recipe reels at about $400 each
consumer.why: A creator who cooks on camera reaches a buying audience for a fraction of a magazine page and leaves the brand a library of recipe video.

consumer.detail: Santo pitched to The Producers and Dirty Linen (one Deep in the Weeds form reaches both), ABC Radio National's Every Bite with Matt Preston, Triple R's Eat It, and ABC Goulburn Murray for harvest-season episodes
consumer.why: Producer-story podcasts are built on exactly this story: three generations, the figs the spec rejected, nothing added.

consumer.detail: Geo-targeted to Victoria, adults 25 to 64 with cooking interests; recipe reels and the store-finder post; retargeting of site visitors
consumer.why: Paid social at this scale does one job: tell people within driving distance of a ranging store that the bottle exists, in the six weeks it is in season.

consumer.detail: Shepparton News (which ran "Giving a fig for heritage" on the farm in April 2024), Shepparton Adviser, ABC Goulburn Murray, WIN News; farm-gate weekends through March; a stall at TatFest, Tatura, Sunday 7 March
consumer.why: Local coverage is free, reliable and read by the Ritchies and IGA shoppers who will see the bottle first.

consumer.tactic: SBS Food, Adam Liaw, Justine Schofield
consumer.detail: Not bought. SBS Media publishes no minimum spend and bars "as seen on SBS" claims; paid product integration needs formal approval. Product offered to The Cook Up's producers as a fig-season ingredient; a quote requested from SBS Media for a small SBS On Demand test in Victoria, held for the extended budget. Justine Schofield (203,000 followers, SBS On Demand series) approached as a gifted send, not a paid post
consumer.why: Television sponsorship starts in the tens of thousands and SBS will not let a brand say it was on air. A pantry mention earned through the producers costs a bottle. The paid option stays in the extended budget where it can be judged against a quote.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.note: Boxes, LinkedIn organic, trade PR, feed build, six tastings run by the family, writer seeding, creator seeding without paid posts, $1,000 of Meta advertising. No harvest lunch coach; writers drive or are hosted overnight.

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.note: Everything in the matrix as costed.

extended.label: Extended
extended.note: Adds a quoted SBS On Demand test in Victoria for the launch fortnight, twelve more tasting days, a paid Inside FMCG feature, a stand at C&I Expo, an Australian Food Awards entry in the syrup class mid-2027 and a Fine Food Australia stand in September 2027.
